evaluation_mode_note: Public Pythonic mode uses the chosen order in ../evaluation-order.md; older ordering rejections below are retained only for the future strict milestone.
numeric_mode_note: Public translation is Pythonic. Exact REAL restrictions below preserve the legacy contract for a future strict milestone; see ../numeric-modes.md.
boundary: Bare ABORT models termination of one offline Python execution only. Exceptions and host snapshots do not implement controller task, motion, handler, restart or persistence semantics.

rules.documented: ABORT terminates task execution and cancels pending/in-progress motion; the statement may specify PROGRAM[n]. Aborted programs cannot resume and must restart. The action and condition forms are separate contexts.
rules.implemented: Only the unqualified ABORT statement in supported program/routine bodies. It raises a distinct KarelAbort exception carrying the source line. IF/SELECT/WHILE/REPEAT/USING and label-dispatched bodies are supported. The dispatcher records ABORT as a terminal node without fall-through.
rules.restriction: PROGRAM[n], arguments, ABORT_TASK, ABORT actions/conditions, condition handlers and NOABORT remain explicitly unsupported. No robot task or motion cancellation is performed.
rules.tests: tests/test_abort.py: syntax, source locations, branches, loops, USING, terminal dispatcher and context guards

rules.documented: The program cannot resume after ABORT and must be restarted.
rules.implemented: An aborted offline Program instance remains terminal. Subsequent run() or generated routine entry raises the original source-located KarelAbort before additional statements or per-run clearing. Constructing a separate Program creates a cold offline instance with uninitialized globals and fresh traces.
rules.restriction: Cold construction is a conservative host contract, not an implementation of controller restart persistence, attributes, scheduler ownership or task status. No resume API or native restart operation is supplied.
rules.tests: tests/test_abort.py: sticky instance, preserved first location, guarded routine entry and independent cold restart

rules.documented: ABORT terminates task execution rather than returning normally from the current routine.
rules.implemented: The exception propagates through nested/recursive generated calls; finally blocks discard local frames. No successful run snapshot is returned. Program.snapshot() supplies copied offline globals and Program.abort_info supplies copied termination metadata. Earlier global/reference writes, delay callbacks and WRITE requests are retained without rollback.
rules.restriction: These are observations of the offline model, not controller post-abort storage or external-effect guarantees. Direct ABORT inside FOR requires fresh routine-local counters; global/reference counters remain blocked because their observable abort state is unvalidated.
rules.tests: tests/test_abort.py and examples/abort_control.kl: nested/recursive cleanup, local FOR, retained effects, defensive observations and distinct runtime failures

rules.implemented: Potential ABORT propagates through call chains and recursion, including skipped branches. Such functions remain blocked in operator expressions/indexed assignments with ambiguous effect ordering. Reports include abort_policy, aborts and routine_effects.*.potential_aborts. Translator --check does not execute ABORT. Generated scripts exit nonzero with KarelAbort; the API caller can catch it explicitly.
rules.restriction: All unreachable source is still checked. Intentional offline termination is distinguished from KarelRuntimeError. No controller status or alarm code is invented.
rules.tests: tests/test_abort.py: transitive effects, source maps, unreachable rejection, translator CLI and generated-script exit
